topics.topic: Claude Code can push a built site live to a public URL
topics.angle: Show the one Claude Code command that takes a site it just built and puts it on a live internet URL for free, using only what Anthropic's own docs confirm it does.
topics.why: YouTube Short on this exact feature got 292,362 views, 9x the channel's usual (InsiderForce), showing strong appetite for a practical Claude Code trick.

topics.topic: TypeScript's baseUrl option is being removed in TS7
topics.angle: Problem: your tsconfig's baseUrl silently breaks path resolution in TypeScript 7; fix: what the official docs say to swap it for.
topics.why: The Stack Overflow question on this exact deprecation has 25,248 views and 4 answers, the highest-traffic candidate in the whole batch.

topics.topic: What actually happens when Claude Code's context window fills up
topics.angle: Myth: Claude Code just keeps remembering everything as your session grows, disproven by what Anthropic's own docs say happens once you near the limit.
topics.why: A YouTube Short about hitting 99% context window got 236,221 views, 9x the channel's usual (Understanding AI HQ), showing this confuses a lot of people using the tool daily.

topics.topic: Prisma v7 upgrade breaks existing projects
topics.angle: Two different-looking Prisma v7 errors (a generic update crash and a '__internal' TypeError) trace back to the same breaking change, so one upgrade-guide fix solves both.
topics.why: Two separate Stack Overflow questions about Prisma v7 errors drew 5,961 and 2,198 views respectively, both within the last two months.

topics.topic: Calling setState inside a useEffect isn't as safe as it looks
topics.angle: Myth: setState inside an effect is harmless because React batches updates, disproven by the new cascading-render warning React itself now throws.
topics.why: The Stack Overflow question quoting this exact React warning has 4,895 views with developers confused about why their effect triggers extra renders.

topics.topic: Should uv.lock be committed or gitignored
topics.angle: Settle whether a Python project's uv.lock belongs in .gitignore using only what Astral's own uv docs say about lockfiles for apps versus libraries.
topics.why: The Stack Overflow question on exactly this has 5,492 views, showing it's a live source of confusion for Python devs adopting uv.

topics.topic: An alpha-only CSS filter still changes your colors
topics.angle: Myth: a CSS filter that only touches opacity leaves your RGB values alone, disproven by how filter compositing actually works per MDN.
topics.why: A Stack Overflow question asking exactly why an alpha-channel filter affects RGB got 1,076 views, a classic 'basics aren't what you think' moment.

topics.topic: Zod's .email() doesn't catch every invalid email
topics.angle: Myth: Zod's built-in .email() validator rejects any bad email string, disproven by the narrower regex Zod's own docs admit it uses on purpose.
topics.why: A Stack Overflow question about unexpected Zod email validation results got 869 views, and Zod schemas are a staple in modern TS/React stacks.

topics.topic: Letting an AI agent rewrite only the slow 5% of your app
topics.angle: Two trending tools this week both skip 'rewrite everything in Rust' and instead have a coding agent port just the hot functions while proving behavior matches the original.
topics.why: Two new GitHub repos built around this exact idea are both trending hard: 8,395 stars and 2,578 stars, each in under 14 days.

topics.topic: Running a big LLM locally on a laptop instead of a GPU server
topics.angle: Problem: everyone assumes a model like GLM-5.2 needs server GPUs; fix: the quantization and serving tricks that let it run on a normal laptop instead.
topics.why: A YouTube Short showing this got 54,453 views (9x the channel's usual), paired with a trending GitHub 'inference optimisation' skill repo (2,026 stars) and a 531-point HN guide to local AI the same week.
